definition: Regular relationships between a resource and performance, and across 3 sources a framing the archive uses more often to check a claimed trend than to establish one. Its positive instance here is unusual: a fitted relationship between policy entropy and downstream performance during reinforcement learning, unchanged across four algorithms, which turns entropy consumption into a predictor of remaining headroom. Its cautionary instances are about scale trends specifically -- one cross-family audit finds an apparent emergence of steerability with model size produced entirely by uncalibrated measurement, and reports its own slope with an interval spanning zero while declining to call the result scale-invariance, noting a homogeneous size axis is itself an assumption and the test underpowered against the slopes the interval admits. The third source gives bounds in the length dimension rather than the parameter one.

evidence.note: Builds a parallel entity grid of 27 folk-narrative motifs across 10 cultures and instruments 18 models with probing, logit lens, activation patching and generation, finding that the residual stream separates cultures cleanly in every model while the readout collapses onto Greco-Roman defaults — so the failure is at the decoder, not the encoder.
evidence.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs

evidence.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
evidence.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

evidence.note: Proves that no computable length-generalization bound exists for transformers of depth two or beyond, and gives a matching exponential bound for the positive fragment that corresponds to fixed-precision transformers.
evidence.title: Length Generalization Bounds for Transformers

name: scaling laws
